Q → bQ | ε
(ii) S → aSb| T
T → bT| ε

Given language:
{aⁿ bⁿ⁺ᵏ | n, k ∈ N}
(i) S → PQ
    P → aPb| ε
    Q → bQ| ε
This is LL(1) (No ambiguity, no left recursion).
To derive ‘ab’:
S → PQ
→ aPbQ
→ ab.
(ii) S → aSb | T
     T → bT | ε

S → aSb
→ aTb
→ abTb (T → bT)

(or)
S → aSb
→ aTb
→ ab(T → ε)
∴ (ii) not in LL(1) (as which production to use in some derivation is unknown).           Choice (A)

question.direction: Directions for questions 1 to 25: Select the correct alternative from the given choices.
question.text:
Consider the following grammar, G:
S → AB
A → aAa | ε
B → bBb | ε
Which of the following statements is TRUE?
(i) G is ambiguous.
(ii) G is not in LL(1).

answer.explanation:
Given grammar G:
S → AB
A → aAa| ε
B → bBb | ε
G is not ambiguous.
(∴ To derive any string only one possible method exists)
G is not in LL(1).
To derive aa.
S → AB
→ aA aB
→ aa A aaB (or) S → AB
(Back track)                  → aA aB
→ aAa B                       → aaB
→ aa                          → aa
∴ G is not in LL(1).
[OR]
To check whether G is in LL(1) or not:
Check whether for all A ∈ N with A → α₁ | α₂ | ... αₙ being all A-Productions in G, the following holds:
(i) FIRST(α₁),………FIRST(αₙ) are pairwise disjoint.
(ii) If ε ∈ FIRST(αⱼ) for some j ∈ [1, n] then FOLLOW(A) ∩ FIRST(αᵢ) = ∅ for all 1 ≤ i ≤ n, j ≠ i.
(i) is satisfied.
FIRST(aAa) = {a}
FIRST(ε) = {ε}
(ii) is failed.
FIRST(aAa) = {a}
FOLLOW(A) = {a, b, $}
These are not disjoint.
∴ G is not in LL(1).                         Choice (B)
